# Judith Chapter 9 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 9

---

## Council Notes

**Key decisions for this chapter:**

**Genre:** This is a petition-prayer in the biblical lament tradition, invoking historical precedent (Gen 34, Simeon) to justify present action. All three translators recognize its intensity.

**v. 2 — "loosened the girdle of a virgin":** EMET preserves the euphemistic Greek idiom (*elusan zōnēn parthenou*). LOGOS follows. PNEUMA paraphrases ("stripped a virgin bare"). The explicit-but-coded Greek idiom must be preserved in SOPHIA: "loosened the girdle of a virgin to defile her."

**v. 4 — "O God, my God — hear me also: a widow":** All three translators handle the climactic self-identification differently. PNEUMA's isolated "I am a widow" is dramatically powerful. EMET's "hear me also — a-widow" is more faithful to the Greek appositive structure. SOPHIA follows EMET's structure but smooths it: "hear me also, O God — a widow."

**v. 7 — "the Lord who crushes wars" / "brings wars to nothing":** The Greek *syntribon polemous* means "crushing/shattering wars." EMET: "who crushes wars." LOGOS: "who brings wars to nothing." PNEUMA: "who unmakes armies." SOPHIA rules: "who crushes wars" — EMET is the most literal and most striking.

**v. 10 — "by the deceit of my lips":** All three render this. SOPHIA notes: Judith explicitly asks God to sanction her deception. This is not incidental — it is the theological crux of her prayer. EMET: "beat-down with my lips and my deceit." LOGOS: "strike down by the deceit of my lips." PNEUMA: "Use my deception." SOPHIA takes LOGOS as the clearest formulation.

**v. 11 — The series of divine epithets:** This verse is a structured hymnic sequence. All three translators render it. SOPHIA takes the clearest English formulation from LOGOS with slight modifications.

**v. 13 — "wound and bruise" / "wound and stripe":** EMET: "wound and a bruise." LOGOS: "wound and a stripe." The Greek *trauma kai mōlōpa* = wound and welt/bruise from a blow. SOPHIA: "wound and a welt" — preserves the physical violence of the imagery.

---

**9:1** Judith fell on her face, put ashes on her head, and exposed the sackcloth she wore beneath. At that very hour the evening incense was being offered in Jerusalem in the house of God. And Judith cried out to the Lord with a loud voice and said:

**9:2** "O Lord God of my father Simeon, to whom you gave a sword for vengeance against the foreigners who loosened the girdle of a virgin to defile her, uncovered her thigh to her shame, and defiled her womb to her dishonor — though you had said it shall not be — yet they did it.

**9:3** Therefore you gave their rulers over to slaughter, and their bed, which was ashamed because of their treachery, you drenched with blood. You struck down slaves together with lords, and lords from their thrones.

**9:4** Their wives you gave over to plunder and their daughters to captivity, and all their spoils were divided among the sons who were dear to you — those who burned with zeal for you and were horrified at the defilement of their own blood, and who called upon you for help. O God, my God — hear me also, a widow.

**9:5** For you accomplished all past things, and the things that followed, and the things present, and the things now being devised. The things that are and the things that are to come you have already planned, and they have come to pass — yes, the purposes you formed in your mind have stepped forward and said: here we are.

**9:6** For all your ways are prepared in advance, and your judgment is with foreknowledge.

**9:7** See — the Assyrians have multiplied in their might; they are exalted in horse and rider; they glory in the strength of infantry; they put their trust in shield and spear and bow and sling. They do not know that you are the Lord who crushes wars.

**9:8** The Lord is your name. Shatter their might by your power and break their strength by your wrath. For they have purposed to defile your sanctuaries, to profane the dwelling place of your glorious name, to cast down with iron the horn of your altar.

**9:9** Behold their arrogance and send your wrath upon their heads. Give into my hand — the hand of a widow — the plan I have formed.

**9:10** Strike down by the deceit of my lips the slave together with his master, and the master together with his servant. Shatter their arrogance by the hand of a woman.

**9:11** For your strength does not rest in numbers, nor your sovereignty in the powerful. You are the God of the humble, the helper of the lowly, the upholder of the weak, the protector of the despairing, the savior of those without hope.

**9:12** Yes, yes — God of my father and God of the inheritance of Israel, Lord of heaven and earth, Creator of the waters, King of all your creation — hear my prayer,

**9:13** and make my word and my deceit a wound and a welt upon those who have devised harsh things against your covenant and your consecrated house and Mount Zion and the house your children possess.

**9:14** And cause every nation and every tribe to know and understand that you are God — God of all power and might — and that there is no one who guards the race of Israel but you."
